question: Find $A^{-1}$, if $A = \begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & 1 \\ 2 & 3 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{bmatrix}$. Hence, solve the following system of equations: $x+2y+z=5$, $2x+3y=1$, $x-y+z=8$.
explanation:
**Step 1:** Find determinant $|A| = 1(3) - 2(2+1) + 1(-3) = 3 - 6 - 3 = -6$.

**Step 2:** Determine the adjoint by finding the cofactor matrix. Co-factors are $C_{11}=3, C_{12}=-3, C_{13}=-3, C_{21}=-2, C_{22}=0, C_{23}=2, C_{31}=-5, C_{32}=3, C_{33}=-1$. $Adj(A) = \begin{bmatrix}3 & -2 & -5 \\ -3 & 0 & 3 \\ -3 & 2 & -1\end{bmatrix}$.

**Step 3:** Form $A^{-1} = \frac{1}{-6} \begin{bmatrix}3 & -2 & -5 \\ -3 & 0 & 3 \\ -3 & 2 & -1\end{bmatrix}$.

**Step 4:** The equations matrix forms $A^T X = B$, where $B = [5, 1, 8]^T$. Therefore, $X = (A^T)^{-1}B = (A^{-1})^TB$.

**Step 5:** Multiply: $X = \frac{1}{-6} \begin{bmatrix}3 & -3 & -3 \\ -2 & 0 & 2 \\ -5 & 3 & -1\end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix}5 \\ 1 \\ 8\end{bmatrix} = \frac{-1}{6}\begin{bmatrix}15-3-24 \\ -10+0+16 \\ -25+3-8\end{bmatrix} = \frac{-1}{6}\begin{bmatrix}-12 \\ 6 \\ -30\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}2 \\ -1 \\ 5\end{bmatrix}$.
